subject: maths
question: Radii of two circles are 20 cm and 4 cm. Length of direct common tangent is 30 cm. What is the distance between their centres?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **Direct Common Tangent (DCT)**, the relationship between **distance (d)**, **radii (R, r)**, and **length (L)** is a **Pythagorean triplet** formed by L, (R − r), and d.

Difference in radii = 20 − 4 = 16 cm

Length of tangent = 30 cm

Distance (d) = √[30² + 16²]

d = √[900 + 256] = √1156 = 34 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of **larger circle (R)** = 20 cm

Radius of **smaller circle (r)** = 4 cm

Length of **direct common tangent (DCT)** = 30 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of DCT = √[d² − (R − r)²]

Where **d** is the **distance between the centers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bd86fecd4be2e48d656005415e85e8c3dde2e2d5ab2e038db1a5af69344e1ab.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 30 = √[d² − (20 − 4)²]

⇒ 30 = √[d² − 16²]

Squaring both sides:

⇒ 30² = d² − 16²

⇒ 900 = d² − 256

⇒ d² = 900 + 256

⇒ d² = 1156

⇒ d = √1156

⇒ d = 34 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of the transverse common tangent is given by TCT = √[d² − (R + r)²], where the tangent crosses the line joining the centers.

Tangent Properties

A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, and for two non-intersecting circles, there are 2 direct and 2 transverse common tangents.

Special Case: Touching Circles

If two circles touch externally, the distance between centers d = R + r. In this case, the length of the DCT becomes 2√(R × r).</p
